title: Complement of a large-diameter graph has small diameter
statement: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set, and let $G^{\mathrm{c}}$ denote its complement, the graph on the same vertices in which two distinct vertices are adjacent exactly when they are non-adjacent in $G$. If the diameter of $G$ is greater than $3$, then the diameter of $G^{\mathrm{c}}$ is less than $3$.
hypotheses_covered: diameter of G is greater than 3
replaced:
\emph{If \texttt{G} has diameter greater than three, then \texttt{G$^{c}$} has
diameter less than three.}
